name: Edinburgh
meta_description: From Old Town pub history to Leith's craft breweries — plan Edinburgh beer tastings, brewery tours and historic pub walks worth booking.
intro_md:
Edinburgh was once one of Britain's great brewing cities, with dozens of breweries at work around 1900, and the trade shaped whole districts. That heritage is still easy to taste. The Old Town's historic pubs cluster along the Grassmarket and Cowgate, the Café Royal's Victorian interior is worth the visit alone, and the Sheep Heid Inn in Duddingston is said to be the city's oldest pub.

The modern scene has settled in Leith. Down towards the water, Newbarns, Moonwake and Campervan all brew within walking distance of one another, and the Shore has become one of Scotland's best places to eat. Back in the centre, Rose Street's pub run and the Bow Bar on Victoria Street cover the traditional end, the latter with a formidable cask and whisky list.

Don't miss:

- Leith's brewery cluster: Newbarns, Moonwake and Campervan
- A pint beneath the Café Royal's Victorian ceilings
- The Bow Bar on Victoria Street for cask ale and whisky
- The Sheep Heid Inn, Edinburgh's oldest pub by repute

gyg_tours.title: Edinburgh: Pub History Tour with Beer & Cider Tasting
gyg_tours.summary: A guided two-hour walk tracing Edinburgh's brewing history from the 1100s to today's craft scene, with tutored tastings of award-winning Scottish beers in three pubs along the way.
gyg_tours.description_md: This guided two-hour walking tour explores Edinburgh's Old Town and its long brewing heritage, tracing how the city grew into a major centre for beer and cider production. Led by knowledgeable local guides, you visit historic and authentic pubs away from the usual tourist spots while hearing stories about the industry's rivalries, expansion and influence on the city. Along the way you taste a selection of award-winning Scottish beers and ciders and learn about the ingredients and science behind brewing.
highlights: Two-hour guided walking tour of Old Town
Tastings of award-winning Scottish beers and cider
Visit authentic pubs beyond tourist areas
Expert local beer-enthusiast guide
Learn Edinburgh's brewing history and heritage
Insights into brewing ingredients and science
gyg_tours.meeting_point: 26 St Giles' Street, Old Town, Edinburgh (the last door at the end of the street next to the railings)

gyg_tours.title: Edinburgh: Underground Beer Tasting in Lost Close
gyg_tours.summary: A tutored tasting of four locally brewed beers held in the Lost Close, a historic underground site in the Old Town, with storytelling about Edinburgh's brewing past.
gyg_tours.description_md:
Join a one-hour guided beer tasting set in an atmospheric underground historic venue known as The Lost Close in the heart of Edinburgh. You will sample four locally brewed craft beers from breweries such as Campervan Brewery, Moonwake Beer Co. and Bellfield Brewery. Throughout the experience, an expert guide shares stories about Edinburgh's history alongside background on each brewery and the flavours in your glass.</description_md>
<parameter name="meeting_point">John's Coffee House & Tavern (part of CoDE Hostel), opposite St Giles' Cathedral and behind the Mercat Cross, marked by the statue of firefighter James Braidwood.
highlights: Taste four local Edinburgh craft beers
Exclusive access to The Lost Close
Atmospheric underground historic setting
Discover Edinburgh's craft beer scene
Led by expert local storytellers

gyg_tours.title: Edinburgh: Leith Brewery Tour and Craft Beer Tasting
gyg_tours.summary: A guided brewery tour in Edinburgh's port district of Leith, covering how the beer is made before a tasting session of the brewery's craft range.
gyg_tours.description_md: Visit a working brewery in Leith, the historic port district of Edinburgh, for a guided tour followed by a tasting in the onsite taproom. You will learn the story of the brewery, the history of brewing in Edinburgh and Leith, and how the port area developed into one of the city's most fashionable neighbourhoods. In the taproom you can sample a range of beers, from familiar styles to more adventurous limited-edition craft brews, whatever your level of experience.
highlights: Guided tour of a Leith brewery
Tasting session in the onsite taproom
Sample beers from familiar to limited-edition
Learn the history of brewing in Edinburgh
Discover Leith's transformation as a port area
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Leith, Edinburgh port area (specific venue not stated)

gyg_tours.title: Leith Brewery Trail: Craft Beers and History Tour
gyg_tours.summary: A three-hour walking trail visiting three of Leith's craft breweries — Newbarns, Campervan and Moonwake — with beer tastings at each stop plus snacks and pizza along the way.
gyg_tours.description_md: This walking tour explores Leith, one of Edinburgh's most vibrant neighbourhoods, combining its history with its craft beer scene. Starting at the top of Leith Walk, you make your way down towards the Shore, Leith's historic port area, passing a Trainspotting filming location along the way. Three local breweries and taprooms are visited: Newbarns, Campervan and Moonwake, each known for a distinct brewing style, with beer samples at every stop. The route concludes near the Scottish National War Memorial.
highlights: Visit three craft breweries and taprooms
Sample beers at each stop
Snacks at the first two breweries
Personal pizza at the final stop
Walk through Leith's historic port area
Gluten-free and vegetarian options available
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Meet by the old cable wheels on Iona Street. The closest tram stop is Balfour Street.

gyg_tours.title: Edinburgh: Harry Potter Walking Tour and Beer Tasting
gyg_tours.summary: A guided walk around the Edinburgh locations associated with J.K. Rowling and the Harry Potter books, followed by a tasting of Scottish beers in an underground cellar with a local expert.
gyg_tours.description_md: This combined walking tour and beer tasting takes you through the Edinburgh locations that inspired J.K. Rowling's writing of Harry Potter, including university sites, historic graveyards and streets. Over roughly two hours, a local guide shares the stories behind Rowling's magical world alongside the wider history of the city. The experience then concludes with a Scottish beer tasting led by an expert in an underground cellar.
highlights: Explore locations that inspired Harry Potter
Visit the Elephant Cafe where Rowling wrote
Five Scottish beer tastings
Tasting in an underground cellar
Views of Edinburgh Castle
Small group with local guide
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Tron Kirk Market on the Royal Mile, opposite Bella Italia (about 10 minutes' walk from Waverley Station)

gyg_tours.title: Edinburgh: The Scotch Whisky Experience Tour and Tasting
gyg_tours.summary: A guided journey through Scotland's five whisky regions beside Edinburgh Castle, ending with a tutored tasting in a vault holding almost 3,500 bottles.
gyg_tours.description_md: At the top of the Royal Mile beside Edinburgh Castle, the Scotch Whisky Experience is the perfect introduction to Scotland's national drink. A guided tour walks you through how whisky is made and matured and takes you on a sensory journey across the country's five whisky-producing regions, before a tutored tasting in the world-famous collection vault — home to almost 3,500 bottles. Named Scotland's Best Visitor Attraction 2024.
highlights: Learn how Scotch whisky is made and matured
Explore the aromas of Scotland's five whisky regions
Tutored tasting in a vault of almost 3,500 bottles
Right beside Edinburgh Castle on the Royal Mile
Award-winning attraction with expert guides
gyg_tours.meeting_point: The Scotch Whisky Experience, 354 Castlehill, top of the Royal Mile, beside Edinburgh Castle

gyg_tours.title: Edinburgh: Holyrood Distillery Whisky & Gin Tour
gyg_tours.summary: A guided tour of Edinburgh's Holyrood Distillery — a modern craft whisky and gin maker minutes from the Royal Mile — with a welcome cocktail and tutored tastings.
gyg_tours.description_md: Holyrood is a modern craft distillery in the heart of Edinburgh, a ten-minute walk from the Royal Mile, making both single malt whisky and award-winning gin. This guided tour takes you through the production areas and the distillery's experimental approach to flavour, with a welcome seasonal cocktail on arrival and tutored tastings of their spirits — including Height of Arrows gin and single malt whisky.
highlights: Guided tour of a modern city-centre distillery
See how both whisky and gin are made
Welcome seasonal cocktail on arrival
Tutored tasting of whisky and award-winning gin
Learn about experimental flavour and cask ageing
Ten minutes from the Royal Mile
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Holyrood Distillery, 19 St Leonard's Lane, Edinburgh
